newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: South Australia to open A$50 mln in contracts.
newsitem.headline: South Australia to open A$50 mln in contracts.

text.p: South Australian government building maintenance and minor works worth up to A$50 million a year would be contracted out to the private sector, the state's contract services minister Dean Brown said on Friday.

Brown said the works would be split into three metropolitan area packages of similar size, with one contract, worth A$15 million to A$17 million a year, awarded to each package for an initial three years with rights of renewal up to seven years.
Individual works within packages would not be worth more than A$150,000 and contractors would be required to deliver most through small business sub-contractors, he said in a statement.

Brown said the contracts would involve 12 government agencies, with building maintenance and minor works worth A$30 million a year and extra facilities management such as cleaning, security and ground maintenance estimated to be worth A$15-20 million a year, he said.
